subject: Archaeology
title: The Venus Figurines
description: A 60-second lesson on The Venus Figurines.

hook.text: Across Europe, archaeologists found dozens of small female figurines with exaggerated features carved 30,000 years ago.

buildup.text: The Venus of Willendorf, found in Austria in 1908, is four inches tall and carved from limestone with no face.

discovery.text: Similar figurines were found from France to Siberia, spanning 10,000 years and thousands of miles.

twist.text: Their meaning is fiercely debated: fertility symbols, self-portraits, goddesses, or something we cannot comprehend.

climax.text: A 2020 study proposed they represent ideal body fat for surviving ice ages — a symbol of health, not beauty.

punchline.text: We call them Venuses. The people who carved them never told us what they meant.

quiz.question: What is one recent theory about the Venus figurines' meaning?
options: They were children's toys traded along migration routes
They represent ideal body fat for surviving ice age conditions
They are portraits of specific tribal leaders
